Results of the Survey on Measuring the Number and Products of Large Livestock (cattle and calves);
Autumn, the year 1401(1)
Definitions and concepts

Agricultural Holding
 It is an economic unit of agricultural production that is run by a single management.

Holding  for raising cattle and calves
 It is an agricultural holding in which  the cattle and calves are raised by using the traditional and modern methods on the enumeration day.

Livestock born alive
 It refers to a calf  that was born alive even though it has died after birth.
Main specifications of the Survey

History 
This survey was conducted for the first time in the winter of the year 1398 on a monthly basis.  Since the year 1399, it has been conducted quarterly.

The Necessity for Conducting the Survey
 Raising large livestock (cattle, buffalo, and camel) is one of the two main activities under the livestock activity section.  According to the results of the  last national census of agriculture,  there are more than 709 thousand large livestock holdings nationwide. 
The most important large livestock  raised in our country is cattle and calf. According to the results of the survey conducted in the year 1399, more than 5.6 million head of cattle and calves are raised in the country. 
The results of the surveys on the livestock shows that 42 percent of the livestock units, 90 percent of the total  produced milk and 56 percent of the weight of red meat come from raising cattle and calves.
With respect to the importance of raising such livestock for providing the food of the community ( red meat and dairy products) as well as its important role in supplying the raw materials for some industries (dairy, food products, and bags and shoes), raising cattle and calves has been always taken into special accounts by the planners in the agriculture sector so that the Ministry of Jihad-Agriculture has always put developing the modern units for raising cattle (modern cattle farms) and breeding such livestock ( aimed at increasing the yield of this type of livestock) in its agenda. This issue has been also included in the National Development Plans.

Overall Specifications of the Survey
Overall objective
 The overall objective of conducting this Survey was to estimate the number of cattle and calves and their main products in the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter.            
Detailed objectives
- Estimation of number and change trend in cattle and calves in the country  by breed in the last month of every season 
- Estimation of the number of calves born alive nationwide in spring, summer, autumn, and winter
- Estimation of cow milk production nationwide in spring, summer, autumn, and winter
- Estimation of  fattened cattle and calves nationwide in spring, summer, autumn, and winter

Winter, the year 1402(1)
Definitions and concepts

Agricultural Holding
 It is an economic unit of agricultural production that is run by a single management.

Holding  for raising cattle and calves
 It is an agricultural holding in which  the cattle and calves are raised by using the traditional and modern methods on the enumeration day.

Livestock born alive
 It refers to a calf  that was born alive even though it has died after birth.
Main specifications of the Survey

History 
This survey was conducted for the first time in the winter of the year 1398 on a monthly basis.  Since the year 1399, it has been conducted quarterly.

The Necessity for Conducting the Survey
 Raising large livestock (cattle, buffalo, and camel) is one of the two main activities under the livestock activity section.  According to the results of the  last national census of agriculture,  there are more than 709 thousand large livestock holdings nationwide. 
The most important large livestock  raised in our country is cattle and calf. According to the results of the survey conducted in the year 1399, more than 5.6 million head of cattle and calves are raised in the country. 
The results of the surveys on the livestock shows that 42 percent of the livestock units, 90 percent of the total  produced milk and 56 percent of the weight of red meat come from raising cattle and calves.
With respect to the importance of raising such livestock for providing the food of the community ( red meat and dairy products) as well as its important role in supplying the raw materials for some industries (dairy, food products, and bags and shoes), raising cattle and calves has been always taken into special accounts by the planners in the agriculture sector so that the Ministry of Jihad-Agriculture has always put developing the modern units for raising cattle (modern cattle farms) and breeding such livestock ( aimed at increasing the yield of this type of livestock) in its agenda. This issue has been also included in the National Development Plans.

Overall Specifications of the Survey
Overall objective
 The overall objective of conducting this Survey was to estimate the number of cattle and calves and their main products in the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter.            
Detailed objectives
- Estimation of number and change trend in cattle and calves in the country  by breed in the last month of every season 
- Estimation of the number of calves born alive nationwide in spring, summer, autumn, and winter
- Estimation of cow milk production nationwide in spring, summer, autumn, and winter
- Estimation of  fattened cattle and calves nationwide in spring, summer, autumn, and winter

Estimating many other statistical items which is related to livestock slaughter such as skin, intestines, head, trotters, and purtenance and/or the number of available livestock throughout the nation.
Using the changes in the average weight of carcass as an indicator to understand the national ranges' status.

Results of the Survey on Measuring the Number and Products of Small Livestock;
Autumn, the year 1401(1)
Topic
Definitions and concepts
Definitions and concepts

Agricultural holding
It is an economic unit of agricultural production that is run by a single management.

Holding raising small livestock
It is an agricultural holding in which  the small livestock are raised by using the traditional and modern methods on the enumeration day.

Livestock born alive
This refers to the lambs and goat kids that were born alive in the enumeration season even though they died after birth.
Main specifications

History 
This survey was implemented with the aim of measuring the monthly changes in the number of small livestock (sheep and goats) in the second half of the year 1397 and the first half of the year 1398, as well as measuring the number and seasonal products of small livestock since the autumn of the year 1398.

The Necessity for Conducting the Survey 
According to the results of the Households Income and Expenditure Survey, over half of  the red meat consumed  by  the households nationwide is related to small livestock. On the other hand, due to the characteristics of small livestock, the population of this type of livestock  has been constantly changing over the year. Availability of timely information on the number of small livestock at different times of the year  is necessary for optimal management of this activity. Moreover, the information on the fattened livestock  is essential to estimate  meat production  for regulating the market of  such a product. Such information plays a very important role in providing animal protein needed by the people of the community and food security. This survey has been implemented with the aim of providing the information needed by planners in the animal husbandry sub-sector, authorities for market regulation of livestock products, all involved in the dairy industry and animal science researchers.

objectives
A. Overall objective
- The overall objective of the implementation of this survey is to estimate the number of small livestock in the months of Khordad, Shahrivar, Azar and Esfand (on the enumeration day) and the quantity of their main products in the spring, summer, autumn and winter.
- Estimation of the "number of slaughtered livestock "sheep and lamb" and "goat and kid" in  the spring, summer, autumn and winter.

B. Detailed objectives
- Estimation of the "number and changes of sheep and lambs"  available in the nationawide livestock in the months of Khordad, Shahrivar, Azar and Esfand (on the enumeration day).
- Estimation of the "number and changes of goats and kids" available in the nationwide livestock in the months of Khordad, Shahrivar, Azar and Esfand (on the enumeration day).
- Estimation of the "number of livestock born, by lamb and goat kids" in the spring, summer, autumn and winter.
-Estimation of the "number of livestock slaughtered, disaggregated by "sheep and lambs" and "goats and kids" in the spring, summer, autumn and winter.

Definitions and concepts

Agricultural Holding
 It is an economic unit of agricultural production that is run by a single management.

Holding  for raising cattle and calves
 It is an agricultural holding in which  the cattle and calves are raised by using the traditional and modern methods on the enumeration day.

Livestock born alive
 It refers to a calf  that was born alive even though it has died after birth.
Main specifications of the Survey

History 
This survey was conducted for the first time in the winter of the year 1398 on a monthly basis.  Since the year 1399, it has been conducted quarterly.

The Necessity for Conducting the Survey
 Raising large livestock (cattle, buffalo, and camel) is one of the two main activities under the livestock activity section.  According to the results of the  last national census of agriculture,  there are more than 709 thousand large livestock holdings nationwide. 
The most important large livestock  raised in our country is cattle and calf. According to the results of the survey conducted in the year 1399, more than 5.6 million head of cattle and calves are raised in the country. 
The results of the surveys on the livestock shows that 42 percent of the livestock units, 90 percent of the total  produced milk and 56 percent of the weight of red meat come from raising cattle and calves.
With respect to the importance of raising such livestock for providing the food of the community ( red meat and dairy products) as well as its important role in supplying the raw materials for some industries (dairy, food products, and bags and shoes), raising cattle and calves has been always taken into special accounts by the planners in the agriculture sector so that the Ministry of Jihad-Agriculture has always put developing the modern units for raising cattle (modern cattle farms) and breeding such livestock ( aimed at increasing the yield of this type of livestock) in its agenda. This issue has been also included in the National Development Plans.

Overall Specifications of the Survey
Overall objective
 The overall objective of conducting this Survey was to estimate the number of cattle and calves and their main products in the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter.            
Detailed objectives
- Estimation of number and change trend in cattle and calves in the country  by breed in the last month of every season 
- Estimation of the number of calves born alive nationwide in spring, summer, autumn, and winter
- Estimation of cow milk production nationwide in spring, summer, autumn, and winter
- Estimation of  fattened cattle and calves nationwide in spring, summer, autumn, and winter

History
The survey on livestock slaughter at national slaughterhouses is one of the current activities of the Statistical Centre of Iran which was carried out annually from the year 1347** to the year 1396 and then it became quarterly as of the year 1396 by changing the implementation method and redesigning of the software. The data collection and dissemination of the survey results are done monthly* since the year 1399.

The Necessity for Conducting the Survey
Whenever the statistical information provided to planners, executive officials and researchers of the country is incorporated with other available information such as geographical distribution, population, imports and exports of livestock and meat products, the following points can be taken into account:

Calculating consumption of red meat per capita as one of the indicators of socioeconomic status.
Estimating many other statistical items which is related to livestock slaughter such as skin, intestines, head, trotters, and purtenance and/or the number of available livestock throughout the nation.
Using the changes in the average weight of carcass as an indicator to understand the national ranges' status.
Planning for importing red meat and its appropriate distribution throughout the nation.
Meeting the statistical needs of economic accounts.
Meeting the statistical needs of other organizations.

History
The survey on livestock slaughter at national slaughterhouses is one of the current activities of the Statistical Centre of Iran which was carried out annually from the year 1347** to the year 1396 and then it became quarterly as of the year 1396 by changing the implementation method and redesigning of the software. The data collection and dissemination of the survey results are done monthly* since the year 1399.

The Necessity for Conducting the Survey
Whenever the statistical information provided to planners, executive officials and researchers of the country is incorporated with other available information such as geographical distribution, population, imports and exports of livestock and meat products, the following points can be taken into account:

Calculating consumption of red meat per capita as one of the indicators of socioeconomic status.
Estimating many other statistical items which is related to livestock slaughter such as skin, intestines, head, trotters, and purtenance and/or the number of available livestock throughout the nation.
Using the changes in the average weight of carcass as an indicator to understand the national ranges' status.
Planning for importing red meat and its appropriate distribution throughout the nation.
Meeting the statistical needs of economic accounts.
Meeting the statistical needs of other organizations.

Definitions and concepts

Agricultural holding
It is an economic unit of agricultural production that is run by a single management.

Holding raising small livestock
It is an agricultural holding in which  the small livestock are raised by using the traditional and modern methods on the enumeration day.

Livestock born alive
This refers to the lambs and goat kids that were born alive in the enumeration season even though they died after birth.
Main specifications

History 
This survey was implemented with the aim of measuring the monthly changes in the number of small livestock (sheep and goats) in the second half of the year 1397 and the first half of the year 1398, as well as measuring the number and seasonal products of small livestock since the autumn of the year 1398.

The Necessity for Conducting the Survey 
According to the results of the Households Income and Expenditure Survey, over half of  the red meat consumed  by  the households nationwide is related to small livestock. On the other hand, due to the characteristics of small livestock, the population of this type of livestock  has been constantly changing over the year. Availability of timely information on the number of small livestock at different times of the year  is necessary for optimal management of this activity. Moreover, the information on the fattened livestock  is essential to estimate  meat production  for regulating the market of  such a product. Such information plays a very important role in providing animal protein needed by the people of the community and food security. This survey has been implemented with the aim of providing the information needed by planners in the animal husbandry sub-sector, authorities for market regulation of livestock products, all involved in the dairy industry and animal science researchers.

objectives
A. Overall objective
- The overall objective of the implementation of this survey is to estimate the number of small livestock in the months of Khordad, Shahrivar, Azar and Esfand (on the enumeration day) and the quantity of their main products in the spring, summer, autumn and winter.
- Estimation of the "number of slaughtered livestock "sheep and lamb" and "goat and kid" in  the spring, summer, autumn and winter.

B. Detailed objectives
- Estimation of the "number and changes of sheep and lambs"  available in the nationawide livestock in the months of Khordad, Shahrivar, Azar and Esfand (on the enumeration day).
- Estimation of the "number and changes of goats and kids" available in the nationwide livestock in the months of Khordad, Shahrivar, Azar and Esfand (on the enumeration day).
- Estimation of the "number of livestock born, by lamb and goat kids" in the spring, summer, autumn and winter.
-Estimation of the "number of livestock slaughtered, disaggregated by "sheep and lambs" and "goats and kids" in the spring, summer, autumn and winter.

Results of the Survey on Measuring the Number and Products of Large Livestock (cattle and calves);
Autumn, the year 1403(1)
Title
Definitions and concepts
Main specifications of the Survey
Definitions and concepts

Agricultural Holding
 It is an economic unit of agricultural production that is run by a single management.

Holding  for raising cattle and calves
 It is an agricultural holding in which  the cattle and calves are raised by using the traditional and modern methods on the enumeration day.

Livestock born alive
 It refers to a calf  that was born alive even though it has died after birth.
Main specifications of the Survey

History 
This survey was conducted for the first time in the winter of the year 1398 on a monthly basis.  Since the year 1399, it has been conducted quarterly.

The Necessity for Conducting the Survey
 Raising large livestock (cattle, buffalo, and camel) is one of the two main activities under the livestock activity section.  According to the results of the  last national census of agriculture,  there are more than 709 thousand large livestock holdings nationwide. 
The most important large livestock  raised in our country is cattle and calf. According to the results of the survey conducted in the year 1399, more than 5.6 million head of cattle and calves are raised in the country. 
The results of the surveys on the livestock shows that 42 percent of the livestock units, 90 percent of the total  produced milk and 56 percent of the weight of red meat come from raising cattle and calves.
With respect to the importance of raising such livestock for providing the food of the community ( red meat and dairy products) as well as its important role in supplying the raw materials for some industries (dairy, food products, and bags and shoes), raising cattle and calves has been always taken into special accounts by the planners in the agriculture sector so that the Ministry of Jihad-Agriculture has always put developing the modern units for raising cattle (modern cattle farms) and breeding such livestock ( aimed at increasing the yield of this type of livestock) in its agenda. This issue has been also included in the National Development Plans.

Overall Specifications of the Survey
Overall objective
 The overall objective of conducting this Survey was to estimate the number of cattle and calves and their main products in the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter.            
Detailed objectives
- Estimation of number and change trend in cattle and calves in the country  by breed in the last month of every season 
- Estimation of the number of calves born alive nationwide in spring, summer, autumn, and winter
- Estimation of cow milk production nationwide in spring, summer, autumn, and winter
- Estimation of  fattened cattle and calves nationwide in spring, summer, autumn, and winter
